text: 1 NC-C function class. Given $\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta>0$ , let $\mathcal{F}(\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta)$ be the union, over all $m,n\in\mathbb{N}$ and all nonempty closed convex sets $\mathcal{X}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}$ and $\mathcal{Y}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{n}$ satisfying $(\mathbf{0}_{m},\mathbf{0}_{n})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\mbox{ and }\operatorname{diam}(\mathcal{Y})\leq D_{\mathcal{Y}},$ of the class of functions $f:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$ satisfying the following properties. For each such function, define $\Phi(\bm{x}):=\max_{\bm{y}\in\mathcal{Y}}f(\bm{x};\bm{y})+\iota_{\mathcal{X}}(\bm{x})$ . 1. ( $\ell$ -smoothness) $f$ is jointly $\ell$ -smooth on $\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ , i.e., for all $(\bm{x}_{1},\bm{y}_{1}),(\bm{x}_{2},\bm{y}_{2})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ , $\left\lVert\nabla f(\bm{x}_{1};\bm{y}_{1})-\nabla f(\bm{x}_{2};\bm{y}_{2})\right\rVert\leq\ell\left\lVert(\bm{x}_{1},\bm{y}_{1})-(\bm{x}_{2},\bm{y}_{2})\right\rVert.$ 2. (Dual concavity) For every fixed $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ , $f(\bm{x};\cdot)$ is concave on $\mathcal{Y}$ . 3. (Initial gap) The initialization satisfies $\Phi(\mathbf{0})-\inf_{\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}}\Phi(\bm{x})\leq\Delta.$

2 Optimization-stationary point. Given $\epsilon>0$ , a point $\bm{x}\in\mathcal{X}$ is an $\epsilon$ -optimization-stationary point ( $\epsilon$ -OS) of Problem ( P ) if $\left\lVert\nabla\Phi_{\frac{1}{2\ell}}(\bm{x})\right\rVert\leq\epsilon,$ where $\Phi_{1/(2\ell)}(\bm{x}):=\min_{\bm{z}\in\mathbb{R}^{m}}\{\Phi(\bm{z})+\ell\lVert\bm{x}-\bm{z}\rVert^{2}\}$ is the Moreau envelope of $\Phi$ with parameter $1/(2\ell)$ .

3 First-order saddle oracle. For a differentiable function $f:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\to\mathbb{R}$ , the first-order saddle oracle at $(\bm{x},\bm{y})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ returns $\mathbb{O}_{f}(\bm{x};\bm{y}):=\bigl(f(\bm{x};\bm{y}),\nabla_{\bm{x}}f(\bm{x};\bm{y}),\nabla_{\bm{y}}f(\bm{x};\bm{y})\bigr).$

4 Zero-respecting first-order algorithm. A first-order algorithm $\mathsf{A}$ is zero-respecting if, for each such $f$ , it starts from $(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(0)}[f],\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(0)}[f])=\mathbf{0}$ and its query sequence satisfies $\operatorname{supp}\bigl(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(t)}[f],\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(t)}[f]\bigr)\subseteq\bigcup_{s<t}\operatorname{supp}\Bigl(\nabla_{\bm{x}}f\bigl(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(s)}[f];\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(s)}[f]\bigr),\nabla_{\bm{y}}f\bigl(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(s)}[f];\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(s)}[f]\bigr)\Bigr),\qquad\forall t\geq 1.$ We denote the class of such algorithms by $\mathcal{A}_{\mathrm{zr}}$ .

5 Deterministic first-order algorithm. A first-order algorithm $\mathsf{A}$ is deterministic if there exists a sequence of maps $\{\Gamma_{t}\}_{t\geq 1}$ such that, for every such $f$ , it starts from $(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(0)}[f],\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(0)}[f])=\mathbf{0}$ and its query sequence satisfies $\bigl(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(t)}[f],\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(t)}[f]\bigr)=\Gamma_{t}\left(\Bigl(\mathbb{O}_{f}\bigl(\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(s)}[f];\mathsf{A}_{\bm{y}}^{(s)}[f]\bigr)\Bigr)_{s<t}\right),\qquad\forall t\geq 1.$ We denote the class of such algorithms by $\mathcal{A}_{\det}$ .

6 Oracle Complexity. Fix $\epsilon>0$ . Let $\mathcal{A}\subseteq\mathcal{A}_{\det}$ be any nonempty subclass of deterministic first-order algorithms, and let $\mathcal{F}$ be a nonempty class of such saddle functions. The oracle complexity of $\mathcal{A}$ over $\mathcal{F}$ is defined by $\mathcal{T}_{\epsilon}(\mathcal{A},\mathcal{F}):=\inf_{\mathsf{A}\in\mathcal{A}}\sup_{f\in\mathcal{F}}\inf\left\{t\in\mathbb{N}_{0}\;\middle|\;\mathsf{A}_{\bm{x}}^{(t)}[f]\;{\text{is an }\epsilon\text{-OS for }f}\right\}.$

7 First-order saddle zero-chain. Let $f:\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}\subseteq\mathbb{R}^{m}\times\mathbb{R}^{n}\to\mathbb{R}$ be differentiable, and let $\bm{\pi}=(\pi_{1},\ldots,\pi_{m+n})$ be a coordinate ordering of $(\bm{x},\bm{y})$ . We say that $f$ is a first-order saddle zero-chain with respect to $\bm{\pi}$ if, for every $i\in[m+n]$ and every $(\bm{x},\bm{y})\in\mathcal{X}\times\mathcal{Y}$ , $\operatorname{supp}_{\bm{\pi}}(\bm{x},\bm{y})\subseteq[i-1]\quad\Longrightarrow\quad\operatorname{supp}_{\bm{\pi}}\bigl(\nabla_{\bm{x}}f(\bm{x};\bm{y}),\nabla_{\bm{y}}f(\bm{x};\bm{y})\bigr)\subseteq[i].$

1 Zero-respecting lower bound. There are numerical constants $c_{0},c_{1}>0$ such that, for every $\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta,\epsilon>0$ satisfying $\epsilon\leq c_{0}\min\{\ell D_{\mathcal{Y}},\sqrt{\ell\Delta}\},$ there exists an instance $f\in\mathcal{F}(\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta)$ for which $\mathcal{T}_{\epsilon}\bigl(\mathcal{A}_{\rm zr}\cap\mathcal{A}_{\rm det},\{f\}\bigr)\geq c_{1}\frac{\ell^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta}{\epsilon^{3}}.$

2 Deterministic lower bound. There are numerical constants $c_{0},c_{1}>0$ such that, for every $\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta,\epsilon>0$ satisfying $\epsilon\leq c_{0}\min\{\ell D_{\mathcal{Y}},\sqrt{\ell\Delta}\},$ one has $\mathcal{T}_{\epsilon}\bigl(\mathcal{A}_{\rm det},\mathcal{F}(\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta)\bigr)\geq c_{1}\frac{\ell^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta}{\epsilon^{3}}.$

1 Arbitrary deterministic output. Theorem 2 also covers a deterministic point computed from the final transcript but not previously queried. Indeed, append that primal point, paired with the feasible dual origin, as the algorithm’s next query and apply the lower bound for queried points to the augmented deterministic algorithm.

3 Oracle complexity of Tracked-FOAM . Let $\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta>0$ and $f\in\mathcal{F}(\ell,D_{\mathcal{Y}},\Delta)$ . For any $\epsilon>0$ , Algorithm 1 , initialized at $\bm{z}^{0}=\mathbf{0}$ , returns an $\epsilon$ -OS point using $\mathcal{O}\left(\left(\frac{\ell\Delta}{\epsilon^{2}}+1\right)\max\left\{1,\frac{\ell D_{\mathcal{Y}}}{\epsilon}\right\}\right)$ (3) first-order saddle-oracle calls.

2 . In the regime of Theorem 2 , the upper bound in ( 3 ) simplifies to $\mathcal{O}(\ell^{2}D_{\mathcal{Y}}\Delta/\epsilon^{3})$ . Thus, Tracked-FOAM is optimal among deterministic first-order methods up to universal constants in this regime.

3 Extensions to other stationarity notions and NC-SC problems. With suitable parameter choices and initialization, Tracked-FOAM also finds an $\epsilon$ -game-stationary point for NC-C problems, as defined in Li et al. (2026, Definition 2.1 (ii)) , with oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\epsilon^{-5/2})$ . This improves the oracle complexity in Li et al. (2026) by removing the multiplicative $\log(1/\epsilon)$ factor. For NC-SC problems, where $f$ is $\mu$ -strongly concave in $\bm{y}$ , Tracked-FOAM can be configured to find either an $\epsilon$ -OS point or an $\epsilon$ -GS point with oracle complexity $\mathcal{O}(\sqrt{\kappa}\epsilon^{-2})$ , where $\kappa:=\ell/\mu$ . Zhang et al. (2021) removed the polylogarithmic factors in $1/\epsilon$ from the bound of Lin et al. (2020a) . Our extension further removes the remaining logarithmic factors in the problem parameters, matching the lower bounds of Li et al. (2021) ; Zhang et al. (2021) in its dependence on $\epsilon$ and $\kappa$ .
